title: bug: the Publish card's Resolve control is refused 403 from the owner's paired browser, so a stuck UNKNOWN publish still has no exit the owner can reach
description:
Found by worker-952c612b on parent task-21be6e9055984413a651ce6ee331e2c8 (step 1, measured in step 2).

THE GAP. The owner's browser authenticates as a paired session: session-authenticator.ts:139 sets principal = sessionId, a durable HUMAN. repository.publish_resolve is operator-only and fences itself (publish-resolve-command.ts:39). It is NOT among the paired-human widenings at daemon-command-registry.ts:441-445, although its sibling repository.publish is. affordance-read.ts still offers it to every reader.

THE EFFECT. A Resolve click answers 403 OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED@DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION with "this command requires the configured operator principal". This is pinned, with a production pairing mint, by the paired-browser dispatch in apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-resolve-journey.test.ts. No other surface reaches the operator principal either:
- the moe CLI's KNOWN_COMMANDS has no resolve command;
- `moe mcp --as-operator` classifies the kind MCP_NEVER_DELEGATED.

THE FIX needs an OWNER ruling. The candidate is to admit a paired durable HUMAN holding ADMIN, on the pattern of release.decide's releaseByPairedAdmin (release-decide-command.ts:77) or goal.cancel's pairedHumanKind, with MCP exclusion unchanged. The fix then flips the journey's paired-browser arm to ACCEPTED.
definitionOfDone: An owner ruling on the widening is recorded on this row before any code changes.

If widened: a paired durable HUMAN holding ADMIN resolves an UNKNOWN publish through the production registry, and publish-resolve-journey.test.ts's paired-browser arm asserts ACCEPTED. A paired HUMAN without ADMIN, and an agent session, are still refused 403 OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED@DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION, each asserted with its code, layer and detail. The kind stays in MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS and MCP_NEVER_DELEGATED_KINDS.

comments.content:
OWNER RULING (DoD 1), given in the architect REPL on 2026-09-19 and recorded by architect-c7fb990e: WIDEN.

A paired durable HUMAN holding ADMIN may dispatch repository.publish_resolve, which makes the Publish card's Resolve control work for the owner's own browser. What does NOT change:
- the kind stays in OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS, so MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS is unchanged (it is derived);
- the kind stays in MCP_NEVER_DELEGATED_KINDS;
- a paired human without ADMIN, and any agent session, are still refused.

The options put to the owner were: widen to paired + ADMIN (chosen); add a `moe` CLI command running as the operator; or move the kind onto `--as-operator`'s delegable list.

IMPLEMENTATION SITE, a correction to the preview shown to the owner. The ruling is unchanged. repository.publish_resolve is an ASYNC registry entry, and async entries are answered before the synchronous handler (daemon-command-registry.ts:379-381). The `pairedHumanKind` widening at :441-445 therefore never runs for this kind. The only operator fence is the entry's own, at publish-resolve-command.ts:39, and the widening goes there. It follows release.decide, the other async operator decision: `assertReleasePrincipal` / `releaseByPairedAdmin` at release-decide-command.ts:66-91 admits operator OR (project match AND ADMIN AND isDurableHumanPrincipal), and fails CLOSED on a throwing read.

DoD 2 LAYER NOTE, measured. This entry's requiredCapability is ADMIN, so a paired human WITHOUT ADMIN is refused at the ingress capability gate (`stage: AUTHORIZE`, `CAPABILITY_DENIED`) BEFORE the entry fence. release-decide-authorization.test.ts:156 shows the same ordering for its capability. The global rail requires asserting the layer that ACTUALLY answers, so that arm asserts CAPABILITY_DENIED@AUTHORIZE at dispatch. The entry fence's own ADMIN conjunct is then defence in depth, pinned by a direct-handler arm that asserts OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED@DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION. An agent session holding ADMIN (minted via session.open, which leaves no durable HUMAN record) does reach the entry fence and is refused OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED@DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION, as DoD 2 says.
